articles.title: Roblox 代价高昂的善意之年
articles.summary: 文章分析Roblox在2026年Q2财报后股价暴跌、市值大幅缩水的深层原因，指出业务增长放缓并非仅因算法调整，而是多重因素叠加，且管理层主动改变加剧了压力。对从业者的价值在于揭示平台型游戏业务在成熟期面临的增长与变现挑战，以及应关注预订量而非滞后收入指标。

games.name: Roblox
games.desc: 多人在线游戏创作平台，用户可自建并分享游戏，以UGC和虚拟经济为核心。

articles.translated_content:
标题：Roblox 代价高昂的善意之年

正文：
Roblox 在 7 月底发布 2026 年第二季度财报后，市值蒸发了近三分之一。该股目前交易价格接近 37 美元，较 2025 年峰值下跌约 75%，也远低于五年前的上市发行价。过去十二个月内，约 700 亿美元市值化为乌有。

Roblox 的业务并未如此惨烈地下滑。第二季度，营收同比增长 36%，日活跃用户（DAU）同比增长 10%。环比来看，营收持平，而 DAU 正在下降。

Roblox 在 2025 年表现非凡，市场以此为标准对其定价。事实证明，管理层也是如此。因此，这是一次预期重置，而非业务失败。这不仅仅是预期问题：Roblox 的增长本已开始降温，与此同时它又开始推行一系列变革，给增长和变现带来了更大压力。更有趣的问题是，这些变革是暂时的自伤，还是恰好落在一个本就在放缓的业务之上。

看预订量，而非营收

Roblox 公布的营收是一个滞后指标。当用户购买 Robux 时，这笔收入会在付费用户的预计生命周期内（根据公司最近一次披露为 27 个月）逐步确认为营收。这意味着 36% 的同比增长只是去年繁荣的回响。预订量——在 Robux 售出时即计入销售额——才是反映当下状况的数字。

第二季度预订量同比增长 8%，但环比下降。困境体现在季度数据上：DAU 已连续三个季度下降，预订量连续两个季度下降，月度唯一付费用户数也随之下滑。每用户支出同样走低，每 DAU 预订量同比下降 2%，每付费用户预订量下降 6%。玩家更少了，每个人的花费也少了。

有三点值得注意：

下滑先于算法变更而存在。
DAU 在 2025 年第三季度见顶，预订量在第四季度见顶。4 月的发现算法更新落在一个本已降温的平台上。

Roblox 在最赚钱的地方表现最差。
美加地区是变现能力最强的市场，那里的预订量与去年同期基本持平。与此同时，欧洲增长 18%，亚太增长 14%，世界其他地区增长 31%。

展望比当季更糟糕。
Roblox 撤回了全年展望，并预计第三季度营收增长 4%–10%，预订量下降 14%–18%。这是该公司首次给出预订量下滑的指引，也是股价暴跌的主要原因。

部分痛楚是自找的

许多最大的逆风源于管理层有意做出的选择。这并不等于这些选择是对的：关键在于今天的增长损失能否为 Roblox 换来未来更强大的平台。

业务正在走向成熟。
没有什么是永远以 20% 的速度增长的。Roblox 公开的目标是占据全球游戏内容营收的 10%。它目前在该市场的份额不足 4%。这既是一笔巨大的业务，也距离目标十分遥远。随着基数变大，这个目标本来就越来越难实现。

2025 年是一个尖峰，而不是一条斜坡。
Grow a Garden 及其后的 brainrot 浪潮打破了同时在线玩家纪录，其变现水平远超 Roblox 可以合理预期复制的程度。娱乐行业是爆款驱动的，平台也不例外。开发者确实在不断进步（当然，现在甚至有了 Grow a Garden 2），但你无法预定闪电。维持 70% 的增长从来都不现实。

安全措施增加了摩擦。
年龄验证于 1 月成为聊天的强制要求。这非常站得住脚，但它确实在新用户与 Roblox 真正核心的社交互动之间多设置了一个步骤。验证还在纸面上缩小了成年受众：一旦年龄经过验证而非自我申报，Roblox 计入的 18+ 玩家占比就降低了。

发现算法现在优化留存。
Roblox 将其“为你推荐”算法从 7 天窗口扩展至 28 天窗口，并分别针对第 1 天、第 2–7 天和第 8–28 天设置了独立信号。Roblox 正在有意将较少玩家导向变现最激进的体验，并表示这对北美 13 岁以下用户支出的影响超出了预期。

发现算法和安全措施，与其说是逆风，不如理解为投资。

安全投入是最明确的一项。目前它是摩擦和法律成本。但从长远看，监管是对 Roblox 征的税，也是对所有更小玩家的壁垒。它也是广告业务的前提条件——你无法在不知道受众年龄的情况下出售定向广告库存。

以参与度为导向的发现算法已有先例。YouTube 在 2012 年从点击量转向观看时长，Google 后来将类似思路应用于 Google Play。在早期，UGC 平台需要供给：更多创作者、更多内容、更多
articles.original_content:
Roblox's Expensive Year of Good Intentions
Skip to content
NAAVIK DIGEST
Roblox’s Expensive Year of Good Intentions
By Miikka Ahonen •   August 16, 2026
Source: Roblo
x
Roblox lost nearly a third of its value after
report
ing
it
s
Q2 2026 results
at the end of July. The stock now trades near $37, about 75% below its 2025 peak and well below its listing price from five years ago. Around $70B in market value has evaporated over the past twelve months.
Roblox's business did not fall as heavily. In Q2, revenue grew 36% and daily active users (DAU) grew 10% YoY. Quarter over quarter, revenue is flat while DAU is declining.
Source: Naavik analysis
Roblox had an extraordinary 2025, and the market priced it for more of the same. So, it turns out, did management. That makes this an expectations reset more than a business failure. It is not
only
an expectations problem: Roblox was already cooling as it began making changes that added even more pressure on growth and monetization. The more interesting question is whether those changes are temporary self-inflicted pain or whether they are landing on top of a business that was slowing anyway.
Look at Bookings, Not Revenue
Roblox's reported revenue is a lagging indicator. When someone buys Robux, that money is recognized as revenue gradually over the estimated lifetime of a paying user (27 months at the company’s last disclosure). This makes the 36% YoY revenue growth an echo of last year's boom. Bookings, which capture the sale when the Robux is purchased, are the number that tells you what is happening right now.
Source: Roblox and Naavik analysis
Bookings grew 8% in Q2 year over year but declined quarter over quarter. The quarterly numbers are where the predicament shows up: DAU has declined for three consecutive quarters, bookings for two, and monthly unique payers have fallen alongside them. Spending per user fell too, with bookings per daily user down 2% YoY and bookings per payer down 6%. Fewer players, each spending a little less.
Three things stand out:
The decline predates the algorithm change.
DAU peaked in Q3 2025 and bookings in Q4. April's discovery update landed on a platform that was already cooling.
Roblox is doing
the
worst where the money is.
U.S. and Canada are the best-monetizing markets, and bookings there stayed essentially flat YoY. Meanwhile, Europe grew by 18%, Asia-Pacific by 14%, and the rest of the world by 31%.
The outlook is worse than the quarter.
Roblox withdrew its full-year outlook and guided Q3 to a revenue growth of 4–10% and a bookings decline of 14–18%. It's the first bookings decline the company has ever guided to, and the main reason the stock crashed.
Some of the Pain is Self-Inflicted
A number of the biggest headwinds are the result of choices management made deliberately. That does not make them good choices: the case rests on whether today’s lost growth buys Roblox a stronger platform later.
The business is maturing.
Nothing grows 20% a year forever. Roblox's stated ambition is 10% of global gaming content revenue. It currently has less than 4% of that market. That is both an enormous business and a long way from the target. The goal was always going to get harder as the base got bigger.
2025 was a spike, not a slope.
Grow a Garden
and the brainrot wave that followed it broke concurrent-player records and monetized far above anything Roblox could reasonably expect to repeat. Entertainment is hit-driven, and platforms are no exception. Developers keep getting better (and of course, there is even
Grow a Garden 2
now), but you cannot commission lightning. Sustaining 70% growth was never realistic.
Safety adds friction.
Age checks became mandatory for chat in January. It’s very much defensible, but it does put an extra step between a new user and the social interaction that Roblox is really about. Verification also shrank the adult audience on paper: the share of players Roblox counts as 18+ was lower once ages were verified rather than self-reported.
Discovery now optimizes for retention.
Roblox expanded its Recommended For You algorithm from a 7-day view to a 28-day view, with separate signals for Day 1, Days 2–7, and Days 8–28. Roblox is deliberately sending fewer players toward the experiences that monetized hardest, and it says the effect on under-13 spending in North America was bigger than expected.
Both discovery and safety are better understood as investments than as headwinds.
Investing in safety is the clearest case. Right now, it is friction and legal expense. But in the long run, regulation is a tax on Roblox and a barrier to everyone smaller. It is also a precondition for the advertising business because you cannot sell targeted inventory against an audience whose ages you do not know.
Engagement-weighted discovery has precedent. YouTube famously shifted from clicks to watch time in 2012, and Google later applied similar thinking to Google Play. Early on, a UGC platform needs supply: more creators, more content, more reasons to open the app. Eventually, a successful platform drowns in content, and the real job becomes deciding what deserves an audience. This is what Roblox is now trying to solve, and what YouTube, Steam, the App Store, and Google Play all went through.
Roblox's platform is unusually vertically integrated. It owns discovery, payments, hosting, identity, and currency. Changing discovery redistributes income across an entire economy, which is why developers spent April watching their impressions move and arguing about whether it was a bug or the point. The question is subtler than "the algorithm hurt me." If distribution now depends on 28-day retention, how does a brand-new game ever prove it has any?
It also makes Roblox game studios harder to invest in or buy. Anyone writing a check wants to know what a game will earn next year, and that guess assumes traffic keeps behaving as it did last year. Roblox has to keep changing discovery, but predictability is worth something too.
A stan
